inspectedText: Rousseau distinguishes copying familiar mature Vermeer paintings from filling a missing early period that scholars expected to find. He discusses provenance, Bredius endorsement, museum purchase and collaboration accusation followed by the confession to forgery and a one-year sentence. He describes hardened resin and old supports as material deception. His account of interrogating Miedl is retrospective participant evidence for his own investigation, not a contemporaneous transcript of Miedl or van Meegeren. His stylistic judgments are interpretation. Specific pigment claims and all reported dialogue are not verified here.
